summary: Iteration 96 (backend only): tested the Admin 'Illustrations IA' endpoints (list, image, regenerate), the extraction of /api/admin/tarot-share/top into admin_viralite.py, the two-tier illustration cache (local disk, then Emergent Storage, then Nano Banana) and the startup prewarm. Admin auth used a real Supabase session for nadine.zebdi@gmail.com, created with tests/_admin_token_helper.py (service-role generate_link + verify). 22/22 pytest passed, including 9 regression tests from iteration 95. The real Nano Banana regeneration of the seeded Alix Ex Libris worked: generation_count went from 1 to 2, last_generated_at moved forward, first_generated_at stayed the same, the bytes changed (21677 to 28830), and the remote Emergent Storage object was overwritten (it matches the local copy). The two-tier cache was verified: with soleil.png deleted and Nano Banana mocked to fail, the JPEG came back from storage with no generation call, and the local file was rewritten. Backend log shows '[prewarm_illust] planets ready: 10/10, closing: True'.

minor.issue: A new AsyncIOMotorClient is created on every request or log call and never closed. This leaks connection pools under load. Reuse the shared db client from server.py or a module-level singleton.

On hot reload or shutdown during the warmup sleep, the log shows a RuntimeWarning: 'coroutine _prewarm_illustrations was never awaited'. This is harmless, because the coroutine object is created before the sleep. Passing a factory (lambda: coro()) would silence it. The same pattern applies to all the other loops.

media_type is always image/jpeg. Old local cache files written before the JPEG migration (.png extension, PNG bytes) would be served with the wrong content-type. Low impact, since current files are JPEG.

_init_storage_sync is called from to_thread workers without a lock (ensure_storage_key is never used by put/get), so concurrent first calls can init several times. Harmless but redundant. The storage_key is also never refreshed if it expires, so later get/put calls will keep failing silently and return None until the backend restarts.

The regenerate call does not check that the hash recomputed from the doc fields equals the path signature_hash. They match today, but if the slug/hash formula changes, the regenerate would write to a different key. Also, there is no rate limit or confirmation on a paid action (~0.02€ per call).

Optional: handle storage_key expiry in emergent_storage (reset _storage_key on 401/403 and retry once)
